title: Create /lets:execute skill
description:
Plan execution skill - takes brainstorm output and implements it in a clean context.

CORE PRINCIPLE: Execute runs in a SEPARATE SESSION from brainstorm. Fresh context = full capacity for code.

Flow:
1. /lets:start picks up task from beads
2. /lets:execute <task-id> loads plan from beads + .lets/plans/<task-id>.md
3. Creates feature branch (feature/<task-id>-<slug>)
4. Reviews plan critically - raise concerns BEFORE starting
5. Batch execution with checkpoints (report progress, wait for feedback)
6. Stop conditions - never force through blockers, ask for help
7. Track progress in beads comments
8. Finish with /lets:check or /lets:review -> /lets:commit -> /lets:end

Key rules:
- Never work on main/master
- Feature branch per task
- Batch execution (default 3 tasks per batch)
- Checkpoint between batches - report + wait for feedback
- Beads comments track progress (not TodoWrite)
- If context runs out mid-execution: /lets:end, new session, /lets:execute continues from beads state

Why separate from brainstorm:
- Brainstorm eats context on exploration, questions, architecture (often 50%+)
- Execute needs clean context for code - reading files, writing code, running tests
- Beads + plan file persist state across sessions
- User reviews plan between sessions (natural checkpoint)

Reference: docs/reference/superpowers-brainstorming-analysis.md

title: Add consistency verification and agent false positive filtering to review
description:
Improve /lets:review command with two changes based on real review experience:

1. Step 5 (agent prompts): Add instruction to all agent prompts: 'Check if the flagged pattern exists in other similar files in the project. If it is a project-wide pattern, flag it as a systemic issue rather than a bug in this PR - still report it, but clearly label it as systemic tech debt affecting multiple places, not a defect introduced by these changes.'

2. New Step 6.5 'Consistency Verification' between Filter (Step 6) and Verdict (Step 7):
- For each finding, check how it is done in other places in the project
- grep analogous files (other services, other components of same type)
- If systemic pattern - keep the finding but downgrade severity and label as 'systemic issue' with note about scope (e.g. 'found in 5 other files')
- If violation of existing pattern - raise severity (this PR deviates from established convention)

Key principle: systemic issues are still surfaced, but clearly distinguished from PR-specific bugs. The review should say 'this is a project-wide pattern worth addressing' not 'this PR has a bug'.

title: Add beads best practices to workflow rules
description:
Add section to hooks/rules-context.md with beads usage rules learned from experience.

Key rules:
1) Epics are containers, NOT blockers - never add epic as dependency for its children
2) Only add dep when task literally cannot start without another being done
3) Use bd dep sparingly - most tasks are independent
4) Parent-child relationship uses --parent flag, NOT bd dep add
5) When creating subtasks under epic, use bd create --parent or bd update --parent
6) EVERY task MUST belong to an epic - no orphan tasks
7) If no suitable epic exists, create one first or add to closest match

Project init workflow:
- When starting a new project, AI and user should plan epic structure together
- Define 3-5 top-level epics covering main work areas
- AI should track existing epics and suggest creating a new epic when tasks don't fit existing groups
- Propose epic when 2+ orphan tasks emerge in the same area

Epic lifecycle:
- Epics are long-lived - they stay open even when all current children are done
- New tasks can always be added to existing epics
- Only close an epic when the USER explicitly says to
- Never auto-close or suggest closing epics just because children are 100% done
- AI monitors epic list and suggests new epics proactively
- Review epic structure periodically (every 5-10 sessions)

title: Create /lets:brainstorm skill
description:
Interactive brainstorming skill - hybrid of feature-dev structure + superpowers brainstorming clarity.

CORE PRINCIPLE: Brainstorm produces a plan and STOPS. No implementation. Clean context boundary - user starts new session for execution.

Phases (from feature-dev, adapted):
1. Discovery - clarify intent via AskUserQuestion
2. Codebase Exploration - lets:* agents (architect, pragmatist) explore context
3. Clarifying Questions - ALL questions at once via AskUserQuestion, WAIT for answers
4. Architecture Design - multiple options via lets:architect + lets:pragmatist
5. Plan Output - save to beads task + .lets/plans/<task-id>.md

Key rules:
- HARD-GATE: no code until plan approved
- Multiple approval gates (not just one)
- AskUserQuestion for structured interaction (multiple choice)
- Scale output to complexity
- Use ONLY lets:* agents
- Output is a PLAN, not code. Plan goes to beads + file.
- Ends with: suggest user to start new session and run /lets:execute

Why separate from execute:
- Brainstorm eats context on exploration, questions, architecture
- Clean context for execute = all capacity goes to code, not 'what did we decide'
- Beads + plan file bridge the gap between sessions
- User gets a checkpoint to review plan before committing to implementation
